name: Dr. Harmon's young orchard by the lake

existence.note: Kinzie, spring 1831: Dr. Harmon 'superintending the construction of a sod fence, at a spot he had chosen, near the shore of the lake. In this inclosure he occupied himself ... in planting fruit stones of all descriptions, to make ready a garden and orchard'. That it still stands in 1835, four seasons on, is inferred. Andreas (1884, vol. 1) gives his 140-acre claim a north line near Sixteenth Street, which is why the plot is just south of that line. The sod fence is not drawn.

clears_local_enu_m.note: The plot and its sod fence, kept clear of the sand hills' dealt cedar, pine and shrubs: a fenced orchard is ground somebody cleared (trees.js inClearedPlot).
